title: High-Frequency DSA Master Bank
disclaimer: These problems are commonly encountered in placement interviews and categorized as high-frequency based on public interview experiences (e.g., LeetCode, GeeksforGeeks, company specific archives). They are NOT guaranteed to be 'the most asked' globally without contextual proof.

problems.problem: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
problems.recognition_clue: Sorted array, finding a pair that sums to target
problems.optimal_approach: Two Pointers starting from left=0, right=n-1
problems.why_optimal_works: Because the array is sorted, we can safely eliminate the smallest or largest remaining element if the sum is too small or too large.
problems.algorithm: 1. Set L=0, R=n-1. 2. Calculate sum=arr[L]+arr[R]. 3. If sum==target, return. 4. If sum < target, L++. 5. If sum > target, R--.
problems.edge_cases: Negative numbers, duplicates that don't sum to target
problems.common_mistakes: Returning 0-indexed instead of 1-indexed (if required by problem variant)
problems.interview_follow_ups: What if the array is not sorted? (Use HashMap)
problems.evidence_note: A highly frequent foundational problem reported across Amazon, Microsoft, and generic campus recruitment drives.

problems.recognition_clue: Finding two lines that form a container to hold maximum area
problems.optimal_approach: Two Pointers at both ends, moving the shorter line inward
problems.why_optimal_works: Area is constrained by the shorter line. Moving the taller line inward can only decrease width without increasing height, so we must move the shorter line to potentially find a taller one.
problems.algorithm: 1. L=0, R=n-1, maxArea=0. 2. maxArea = max(maxArea, (R-L)*min(height[L], height[R])). 3. If height[L] < height[R], L++; else R--.
problems.edge_cases: All heights are the same, minimum required inputs (n=2)
problems.common_mistakes: Moving the taller line inward instead of the shorter one
problems.interview_follow_ups: Can you do this if lines are dynamically added?
problems.evidence_note: Standard visual logic puzzle heavily asked in initial tech screening rounds.

problems.recognition_clue: Finding a 'longest' contiguous substring based on a condition (no repeats)
problems.optimal_approach: Variable-size Sliding Window using a HashSet or frequency array
problems.why_optimal_works: By keeping track of characters in the current window, we can expand right until a duplicate is found, then shrink from left until the duplicate is removed.
problems.algorithm: 1. Use L=0, R=0, maxLen=0, set. 2. If char at R is in set, remove char at L and L++. 3. Else add char at R to set, update maxLen, R++.
problems.edge_cases: Empty string, string with all identical characters
problems.common_mistakes: Forgetting to shrink the window until the *specific* duplicate is removed
problems.interview_follow_ups: Can you optimize this to exactly O(N) by jumping the left pointer using a HashMap?
problems.evidence_note: Consistently ranked in the top 5 most asked string questions globally.
